cases.refreshed: Middle and high schoolers: Come explore the TeenHQ MakerSpace! Up to 5 teens at a time can use our 3D printers, a poster printer, a Glowforge laser cutter, sewing machines and sergers, a Cricut, a button press, and assorted craft supplies. Work with our teen librarian to bring your idea to life. Equipment and materials have limits and time requirements. All services are provided for free to middle and high school students (grades 6-12). Younger people and adults are not permitted in the area unless required to assist with a disability. The area is wheelchair accessible from the Children's Room elevator. Other accommodations can be made available upon request. Please note that each device requires time to set up, use, and complete whatever task you're wanting to use the space for. Be sure that you have enough time in your schedule to attend the program. Not all tasks may be completed before the end of the program and you may need to return to get your completed items or pause your task and restart at another studio session. We appreciate your patience and flexibility. 3D Printing: All requested prints must take less than 4.5 hours to print. All requested prints will need to be picked up at a later date. Contact information is required for notification of pick-up. 3D print quality and the time needed to complete prints are not guaranteed. Multiple objects can be printed as long as the total time does not exceed 4.5 hours. Poster Printing: Set up your design on a 24 × 36-inch canvas and save it as a PNG file. Please see the regularly scheduled poster printing event for further details. One poster per teen per day. Glowforge: Create a custom engraved object. Follow guidelines similar to those for the Custom Keychain Program. The librarian decides how complex a request can be. Sewing & Serger Machines: It is recommended that you bring your own fabric and thread if fabric is special or color is a factor. Scrap material and thread are available, but we cannot guarantee material quality or availability. An iron and ironing board are also available. Cricut: Basic Cricut supplies are available, such as construction and cardstock paper. If your project is specialized, such as requiring iron-on, you'll need to bring your own materials. It is recommended that you know the requirements for any materials you provide. Button Press: TeenHQ offers two sizes of button presses. We cannot offer printing. If you bring your own printout of buttons, it must be printed on standard printer paper. Paper thicker than standard printer paper cannot be used on the button presses. All measurements below are diameters in inches. Small Button Press: 1.25"; Large Button Press: 2.25"; Picture Size: 1.156"; Cut Line: 1.629"; Picture Size: 2.063"; Cut Line: 2.625".

cases.refreshed: Experience the soothing calm of yoga and meditation, as presented by our partner, The Heartfulness Institute, each Saturday. Yoga is taught by certified instructors and meditation is taught by a Heartfulness-certified instructor. Yoga may be either chair or regular yoga. The program structure is 75 minutes as described below: 5 min: Meet & greet; 35 min: Yoga and Pranayama (different styles like hatha or arkaya yoga); 5 min: posture change break; 25 min: Heartfulness Relaxation & Meditation (experience, hands-on). This program is geared to enrich the lives of adults and seniors. Please note that all new participants will need to complete the Exercise Waiver in order to be able to participate. The Exercise Waiver must be completed before your first day of participation. Exercise Waivers will be provided at each meeting.

cases.refreshed: This event was rescheduled from November 22. Join us for the Julia Robinson Math Festival, an event that provides students with fun and meaningful math experiences to develop their mathematical confidence, joy, and problem-solving skills. There will be a variety of play-based, manipulative-based math puzzles and games for students in grades K - 8 and their parents or caregivers. Each activity will be led by at least one trained volunteer who will introduce the activity and keep students engaged and excited as they explore. The festival will be open for 1 hour, during which time kids will get to explore the festival at their own pace, choosing where they want to go and for how long they want to do each activity. Recommended for ages 5 to 10+. Free. No registration required. This program is brought to you by the San Jose Legacy Youth Foundation.

events.title: Everyone Can Create: Beginning Stop Motion Animation

cases.refreshed: Learn how to use the Stop Motion Studio app to make simple stop motion animations using small toys and paper. Participants will have an opportunity to showcase their work at the end of the session. iPad devices will be provided to all participants. Recommended for children ages 6 to 12. The theme of all five classes in November is Thanksgiving/Fall: November 1 - Introduction to Stop-Motion Animation. Children will learn how stop-motion animation works and create their own Thanksgiving/Autumn props and characters for their movie. November 8 - Creating the Thanksgiving Story. Children will develop their Thanksgiving story and begin planning the scenes, characters, and settings for their movie. November 15 and 22 - Filming the Movie. Children will use their characters and props to film their Thanksgiving movie, learning how to move objects and characters frame by frame. November 29 - Finishing the Movie. Children will complete their animation, add final details, and watch their Thanksgiving movies come to life! Free. Registration required.
